thread:
Mia: Heads up, brought a new model through onboarding today (larch-7m-mod). License has a few odd clauses, need quick sanity check before we run large quant experiments.
Sam: summary?
Mia: key bits: 'NonCommercial: no direct commercial exploitation', 'Attribution: must display exact text in UI and docs', 'Redistribution: derivative weights allowed but only if upstream credited and not rehosted as a competing service'. Also a paragraph about 'modifications allowed' and 'no sublicense'.
Elena: ugh that rehosted-as-competing-service line is vague. Are we allowed to serve it via Hosted API or Dedicated for customers who pay? That's basically our product.
LegalBot: quick note: licenses with "NonCommercial" typically prohibit commercial usage unless you obtain a separate license. "Not rehosted as a competing service" is enforcement language—interpretation depends on whether you act as a reseller or just provide inference. Need to see full license text. Upload the license snippet?
Mia: pasted the section:
```
Redistribution and Derivative Works: You may modify and redistribute derivative weights provided you (i) retain attribution to the original authors ("Larch Project"), (ii) do not sublicense the derivative model such that it enables a third party to operate a publicly hosted inference service that competes with the original model host, and (iii) inform the original authors of any public release.
```
Raj: test plan: we want to run int8/4-bit quant experiments, store quantized artifacts in our internal model registry, and occasionally provide snapshots to Dedicated customers' VPCs and to on-prem packages. The question is: does handing a dedicated customer a copy count as 'redistribute' or is that allowed as part of a paid product? Also, if customer hosts in their own infra, are we still 'sublicensing'?
Ciara: for Dedicated we typically push the image/weights into a customer-managed bucket or their VPC. We're not providing public inference endpoints on hosted tier for that customer—it's isolated. That feels different than a public hosted API.
LegalBot: nuance: providing a customer with a copy of the weights is redistribution. If the license forbids redistribution to enable a competing hosted service, that's a narrower restriction. But a clause that forbids rehosting in any 'competing' situation could be broad and risky. Two paths: 1) contact upstream for a commercial/enterprise license clarifying redistribution to customers for Dedicated/on-prem; 2) treat non-hosted, customer-managed deployments as permissible (less risk) but avoid offering hosted inference on the shared Redwood Hosted API without explicit permission.
Sam: what about attribution text? They insist exact wording be shown in UI and docs. Do we embed into SDK responses or link in model card?
Elena: they require exact wording: "Model: Larch 7M (Larch Project). Original weights and training data credited to Larch." They also say "attribution must be visible to end users of any derived or hosted model".
Mia: totally feasible to put in model card and Dedicated onboarding docs. But for Hosted API where we stream tokens, we don't have a canonical UI surface for every API consumer—some apps embed responses without our UI.
LegalBot: best practice: add required attribution to the model card and to any product-facing UI where the model is explicitly surfaced. For Hosted API, include attribution in the developer dashboard, the API response metadata when model is requested (e.g., in response.headers or in response.metadata), and in default SDK examples. But if downstream customers remove attribution from their product, the downstream relationship is between them and the license; we should advise customers of their obligations and require them to accept the license in the Dedicated/on-prem terms.
Raj: about quantized weight redistribution: often quantized weights are considered derivative. If redistribution of derivatives is allowed but with attribution, we can share quantized blobs with customers if we comply. The risky bit is providing a copy to external third parties who then host public endpoints for others. We should probably add a Customer Terms clause that prohibits customers from rehosting as a public generic inference service.
Ciara: we already have an AUP for Dedicated customers that forbids building multi-tenant public AI hosting services on top of Dedicated instances. Could reuse that. Still, ops needs a checklist: when onboarding a model with NonCommercial or ambiguous redistribution lines, we should block Hosted API placement until legal OK.
Mia: action items proposal:
- Legal: confirm whether providing a copy of quantized weights to a paying Dedicated customer violates the redistribution clause, or if it's permitted when the customer is the licensee. If not permitted, ask upstream for a carveout.
- Product/Platform: add automatic attribution insertion to model card + API metadata and update Dedicated onboarding checklist to flag 'NC' or 'restrictive redistribution' models.
- Eng/ML: hold off public Hosted placement and mass quantized artifact publishing until legal greenlight.
Sam: +1. Also, can we add a technical mitigation: only allow shipping weights to customers after a click-through that includes the original license text and requires confirmation they will not rehost as a competing service.
LegalBot: sounds good. I'll draft an outreach template to upstream maintainers asking for explicit commercial redistribution permissions for enterprise customers and a defined attribution snippet. Also recommend we treat "NonCommercial" as blocking for Hosted API until we get a commercial license.
Elena: thanks. one more edge case: model card data retention / telemetry. License mentions authors must be informed of any public release—does that include internal benchmarking or evals? We do a lot of private evals.
LegalBot: "inform the original authors of any public release" typically means publishable releases. Internal benchmarks and private evals are fine. When we publish benchmark results or a derivative publicly, include a notice and link to upstream.
Mia: perfect. I'll pause the Hosted rollout and mark the ticket with legal-blocker. Thanks all :thumbsup:
